package_info.package_manager: unmanaged (C/C++ library, also distributed via OS package managers and bundled in other software)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of libwebp contain a critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability that can be triggered by processing a specially crafted .webp image. This allows attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause denial of service, making the package dangerous when used in any software that processes untrusted .webp images.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a .webp image is processed by the application)
execution_context.file_location: libwebp core image parsing routines (e.g., src/dec/vp8l_dec.c or similar internal decoder files)
required_permissions: potentially network (if images are fetched remotely)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a specially crafted .webp image is parsed, the code allocates a buffer based on image metadata, then copies image data into this buffer without proper bounds checking, allowing heap-based buffer overflow and potential arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fails to properly validate the size of the input data against the allocated buffer, allowing an attacker to craft an image that causes memory corruption.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Image parsing libraries are expected to validate all input sizes and prevent overflows; this code allows attacker-controlled data to exceed buffer boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate image decoders allocate buffers and copy data, but always with strict bounds checking based on validated image headers.
key_indicators: Buffer allocation based on untrusted image metadata
Lack of bounds checking before memcpy/memmove

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious .webp image with manipulated metadata to trigger the overflow.
attack_chain.leads_to: Image is delivered to the target application (e.g., via web, email, or file upload).

attack_chain.action: Target application processes the malicious .webp image using a vulnerable version of libwebp.
attack_chain.leads_to: Heap-based buffer overflow is triggered during image parsing.

attack_chain.action: Overflow allows attacker to corrupt memory, potentially leading to denial of service or remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution or causes application crash.

behavioral_signatures: Heap-based buffer overflow triggered during .webp image parsing
Crash or abnormal termination of processes handling .webp files
Unexpected memory corruption or access violations in image processing routines
file_indicators: Presence of .webp files with abnormal or oversized metadata fields
Unusual .webp files received via untrusted channels (web, email, uploads)
network_indicators: Delivery of .webp files from suspicious or untrusted sources
Repeated access to .webp files immediately preceding application crashes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for application crashes or memory access violations when processing .webp images, especially in software using libwebp versions 0.5.0 to 1.3.1. Use static analysis or binary scanning to identify vulnerable libwebp versions in deployed software. Employ fuzzing or dynamic analysis to detect abnormal behavior when opening .webp files. Flag .webp files with unusually large or malformed metadata for further inspection.
